record.title: China opens 2026 green-compute facility recommendations with energy, carbon, water and utilization criteria
record.summary: A five-agency Chinese notice opens recommendations for 2026 national green-compute facilities. It requires at least one year of stable operation, specified energy-efficiency and green-data-center levels, renewable-electricity share at least the provincial responsibility weight, and measured energy, water and compute-utilization information; ordinary facilities generally need at least 3,000 standard racks and 60% rack occupancy, with stated exceptions. Applications are due 16 November 2026 and the agencies say they will review submissions before publishing a recommended list. These are eligibility and screening rules, not evidence of facility compliance, selection outcomes or improved AI-compute economics.
organizations: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: Five Chinese agencies published a 2026 national green-compute-facility recommendation notice on 2026-09-21, with submissions due by 2026-11-16.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice requires stable operation, specified efficiency and green-data-center criteria, provincial renewable-electricity-share thresholds and resource-use information; most ordinary facilities face thresholds of at least 3,000 standard racks and 60% rack occupancy, with listed exceptions.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice provides for agency/expert review and says prior-year shortfalls on key indicators can lead to removal from the list; it does not report 2026 applicant-level results or measured policy effects.

evidence_gaps.description: No published 2026 applicant roster, expert decisions or facility-level audited KPI values.

brief.importance_rationale: If applied to a substantial share of compute facilities, the requirements could affect investment and operating priorities across energy, carbon, water and compute utilization. The notice establishes screening rules and a review process, not measured compliance or causal impact.
limitations: The notice specifies a recommendation process and eligibility conditions but provides no applicant list, facility-level measurements, audit decisions or post-policy outcomes.
The official scoring attachment and separate self-evaluation forms describe measurement and reporting; the notice does not establish their implementation quality.
Any effect on AI-compute availability, cost or workload quality remains unmeasured.

technical.claimed_result: The agencies state that selected facilities will meet the specified green-compute requirements; no 2026 selections or compliance outcomes are yet reported here.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official Chinese-language notice directly establishes the criteria, process, deadline and stated removal rule. It supplies no facility outcome measurements.
technical.mechanism: Establishes eligibility, self-assessment, provincial/agency recommendation and five-department review for annual national facility recommendations.
technical.regime: 2026 national recommendation process covering compute facilities across sectors in China; submission deadline 2026-11-16.
technical.strongest_baseline: The notice references earlier green-compute facility batches but does not compare measured performance or policy effects.

brief.title: China opens 2026 green-compute facility recommendations with energy, carbon, water and utilization criteria
brief.why_it_matters: The criteria make energy, water, renewable electricity and resource utilization part of a national compute-facility recommendation process. They may shape which facilities qualify for recognition, but the notice alone does not show adoption, verified performance or the effect on available AI compute.
